title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
Scammers deployed AI-generated video and image synthesis to create fake social media profiles impersonating a real immigration attorney, Angel Leal. The system generated hundreds of fraudulent accounts across multiple platforms with AI-synthesized content showing the attorney promoting services he does not offer. This is impersonation at scale, enabled by generative AI tools that produced realistic enough deepfakes to deceive vulnerable people seeking immigration assistance.

The fraud operated without any human verification step on the platforms hosting it. Scammers directed victims from social media videos to WhatsApp and payment apps, where they collected money for fake legal services using fabricated contracts. The scheme targeted immigrants specifically, exploiting their need for legal help and language or information barriers that made verification harder.

It is not established who created or deployed the generative AI systems, what tools were used, or whether the platforms' own systems detected and failed to remove the content before Leal's firm hired outside help to take action.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, discovered that criminals are using artificial intelligence to impersonate him and defraud vulnerable immigrants. Scammers created hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles featuring AI-generated images of Leal promoting immigration services he never offers. In one scheme, the fake Leal promises US residency assistance to undocumented immigrants for $2,200. The fraud escalated dramatically over the past three months after potential clients began calling his office about these bogus offers.

Leal's firm hired an online anti-piracy company that has removed nearly 6,500 fraudulent accounts across social media platforms, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The scams typically start with social media videos directing people to contact a WhatsApp number, where fraudsters send fake contracts and collect money through payment apps like Venmo and Zelle. Leal warns immigrants to verify anyone offering legal services online and avoid those requesting immediate payment through digital platforms. He plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the scams.
